organization.name: imd
organization.title: IMD
organization.description:
India Meteorological Department was established in 1875. It is the National Meteorological Service of the country and the principal government agency in all matters relating to meteorology and allied subjects.

1.  To take meteorological observations and to provide current and forecast meteorological information for optimum operation of weather-sensitive activities like agriculture, irrigation, shipping, aviation, offshore oil explorations, etc.
2. To warn against severe weather phenomena like tropical cyclones, dust storms, heavy rains and snow, cold and heat waves etc. which cause destruction of life and property.
3. To provide meteorological statistics required for agriculture, water resource management, industries, oil exploration and other nation-building activities.
4. To conduct and promote research in meteorology and allied disciplines.

organization.description:
Tripura has both surface water and groundwater management entities overseeing water resources in the state.

For groundwater management, the Central Ground Water Board (CGWB) has assessed and managed Tripura's groundwater resources. The state experiences a varied hydrogeology, with aquifers mainly occurring within the Tipam and Dupitila formations. Groundwater is generally found under unconfined conditions in these formations, and deeper zones show semi-confined to confined characteristics. The state's overall groundwater extraction is low, with all 59 assessment units categorized as "Safe," meaning extraction levels are sustainable.

For surface water, the Tripura Jal Board, established under the Tripura Jal Board Act, 2020, is responsible for water supply and sewerage systems, particularly in urban areas. The Board aims to streamline water supply services and control the wastage of water. As the state faces drinking water shortages, this body enforces regulations to ensure sustainable water use​.

In Mizoram, groundwater management and regulation are overseen by the Mizoram Ground Water Authority (MGWA), which was established under the Mizoram Ground Water (Control and Regulation) Act, 2023. This law mandates that any individual or entity wishing to extract groundwater must obtain permission from the state authorities. It aims to ensure sustainable groundwater use and prevent over-extraction, particularly in light of growing concerns about aquifer depletion and land subsidence. The Act also requires users to register existing wells and drilling agencies.
In addition, the law emphasizes rainwater harvesting and artificial recharge to groundwater through measures like check dams, weirs, and the development of springs.

organization.name: uttarakhand
organization.title: Uttarakhand SW GW
organization.description:
In Uttarakhand, surface and groundwater management is overseen by several key agencies. The State Water & Sanitation Mission (SWSM) plays a crucial role in managing water resources, especially in rural areas. The mission is responsible for providing clean drinking water and managing sanitation services across the state. It implements various programs to improve water supply infrastructure, promote sustainability, and enhance community participation in water management​.

Regarding groundwater, the Central Ground Water Board (CGWB) collaborates with state authorities to assess and manage groundwater resources. Groundwater in Uttarakhand is primarily sourced from springs, especially in the mountainous regions, and is used extensively in agricultural and domestic applications. As of the latest assessments, the total annual groundwater recharge is estimated at 2.02 billion cubic meters, with an annual extraction of 0.95 billion cubic meters. The majority of the state is categorized as having "Safe" groundwater resources, with 22% of the state being in a "Semi-Critical" category​.
